{"rewrites":[{"transformation":"Converts the correlated EXISTS semi-join (SELECT $2 ... WHERE li.product_id = p.id AND ...) into an uncorrelated IN semi-join: p.id IN (SELECT li.product_id FROM line_items li JOIN orders o ON o.id = li.order_id WHERE <same filters>). The correlation predicate becomes the IN comparison, and the unused constant select-list item $2 is dropped. The rewrite also renumbers the placeholders: its $2 is the original $3 (o.created_at bound, timestamptz) and its $3 is the original $4 (li.quantity bound, integer). To return the same rows, it must be bound with the original $3 and $4 values in those positions; binding the original numbering would compare created_at with the integer $2. In a WHERE clause, a positive IN is equivalent to EXISTS even when NULLs are present, because a NULL result is filtered out exactly like false. So no schema assumptions are required.","assumptions":[]}]}
